summary: Updates the base specifications for Certificate Management over CMS (CMC), updating RFC 5272, RFC 5273 and RFC 5274. It adds new controls for generating keys on the server side, a way to identify CMC servers, and registers a TCP port for the service. It was later replaced by RFC 10002, RFC 10003 and RFC 10004.

eli5.summary: A certificate is like an ID card for computers, and CMC is the paperwork to get one. This adds a few new forms and a standard place to ask, then was later replaced by newer papers.

subtitle: Enhanced controls and attributes for certificate management

tldr.problem: The base CMC (Certificate Management over CMS) specification lacked certain controls and attributes needed for practical deployment, particularly for server-side key generation and improved identity verification.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 6402 adds new controls for RA identity verification, response body handling, a new attribute for name changes, Extended Key Usage values for different CMC server types, a Subject Information Access extension to locate CMC services, and registers TCP port 5318 for CMC.
tldr.outcome: CMC deployments gained essential features for delegation of identity proofing to registration authorities and support for future server-side key generation. It was replaced by more comprehensive updates in RFC 10002, RFC 10003, and RFC 10004.

today: RFC 6402 is classified as a Proposed Standard and is still in use. However, its updates to RFC 5272, RFC 5273, and RFC 5274 have themselves been superseded by RFC 10002, RFC 10003, and RFC 10004, which provide more comprehensive updates to the CMC specifications.

sections.title: Introduction and Updates Overview
sections.content:
RFC 6402 contains a set of updates to the base Certificate Management over CMS (CMC) specification, which is defined in RFC 5272, RFC 5273, and RFC 5274. These updates address deficiencies discovered while developing the Suite B profile of CMC.

The key additions include new controls for RA operations, a Subject Name Change attribute allowing clients to request name modifications, Extended Key Usage values to distinguish different CMC server types (CA, RA, Archive), a Subject Information Access extension for locating CMC services, and registration of TCP port 5318 as the standard port for CMC over TCP/IP.
sections.eli5: This updates the certificate request system to work better. It adds new instructions for different steps of the process and a standard phone number (port) for the service.

sections.title: New Controls and Attributes
sections.content:
Two new controls enhance the CMC protocol's capabilities for complex deployments. The RA Identity Proof Witness control (id-cmc-raIdentityWitness) allows a Registration Authority to indicate that all identity proof requirements have been met, shifting identity verification responsibility closer to the end-entity. This permits a distributed deployment where physical locations perform identity checking while a central CA only needs to validate that the RA performed proper verification.

The Response Body control (id-cmc-responseBody) enables an RA to embed a nested response message within its own response for an end-entity to process. This is particularly useful when an RA performs key generation on behalf of an end-entity and must return both the CA's issuance response and the newly generated key material.

A new ChangeSubjectName attribute lets clients request changes to the subject name and subject alternative name fields in certificates. This attribute can appear in PKCS #10 or CRMF certification requests and provides security by requiring the CA to verify proper identity before allowing name changes.
sections.eli5: The system now lets a local office check someone's identity and tell the main office "yes, this person is real," without sharing the secret used to check them. It also lets people ask to change their name on the certificate when they request it.

sections.title: Server Identification and Certificate Extensions
sections.content:
CMC server certificates now use Extended Key Usage (EKU) extensions to clearly identify their role. Three EKUs are defined: id-kp-cmcCA for certification authorities, id-kp-cmcRA for registration authorities, and id-kp-cmcArchive for archive servers. These extensions restrict a certificate's use to specific CMC operations, improving security by preventing misuse of certificates intended for one role in another role.

The Subject Information Access (SIA) extension identifies how to contact a CMC service. The new id-ad-cmc access method allows a CMC certificate to publish its service locations using URIs (for HTTP/FTP), email addresses (for mail), or domain names and IP addresses (for TCP/IP). TCP/IP-based CMC services use port 5318 by default, now officially registered with IANA for the pkix-cmc service.
sections.eli5: Server certificates now include information about what job they do (CA, RA, or Archive) and how to reach them. TCP/IP services use a standard port number (5318) so clients know where to look.

sections.title: Attributes and Linking Requirements
sections.content:
RFC 6402 clarifies the placement of attributes in CMC messages. Attributes can appear in the attribute sequence of a PKCS #10 request, in the controls field of a CRMF request, or in various CMS attribute sequences. The ChangeSubjectName attribute provides a standardized way to request name modifications while maintaining proper linking between identity proof and proof-of-possession information.

The specification expands the concept of existing certificate linking beyond just renewal and rekey operations. A certificate can now be used to link identity and possession proofs in three scenarios: renewing or rekeying an existing certificate, obtaining a new certificate type with the same identity, or using a pre-distributed device certificate to prove identity to a CA. This flexibility enables more deployment scenarios while maintaining security through proper linking of identity and possession proofs.
sections.eli5: The system now has a clear way to say "I want to change my name" in the request. And instead of just using your old certificate to renew it, you can use an old certificate for lots of other requests too.

sections.title: Operational Considerations and Future Work
sections.content:
RFC 6402 registers TCP port 5318 for CMC operations under the service name pkix-cmc. While HTTP remains the primary transport method for most CMC deployments, this registration provides a standard port for organizations implementing direct TCP/IP transport. The specification notes that client implementations may continue to support externally configured ports for backward compatibility, but server implementations are encouraged to migrate to the standard registered port.

The updates also lay groundwork for future server-side key generation. The controls and attributes defined here support scenarios where an RA generates keys on behalf of an end-entity, a capability that will be more fully developed in future specifications. The framework established by RFC 6402 ensures that key generation operations can be properly linked to identity verification and that responses containing generated keys can be properly delivered to the requesting end-entity.
sections.eli5: If you want to use plain TCP instead of web protocols, use port 5318. The updates also prepare for a future where servers can create new keys for you, which will be explained in later documents.
